approach: Widen the planning gate in `Athena::dispatch` (crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:804-809). Add a private, doc-commented helper `asks_for_failing_run(&Reading) -> bool`. It is true when any accepted Behavior criterion's text (lower-cased, whitespace collapsed) contains one of four fixed phrases: `fails without the fix`, `fail without the fix`, `fails without the change`, `fails without the mechanism`. Pass `reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_failing_run(&reading)` to the existing `JobPlanConfig::plans`. `plans` keeps its `enabled && (All || hard)` rule and the `!capability.pins_repo()` guard stays, so `enabled = false`, `mode = "all"` and the study exception behave as before. A newly planned job follows the existing path (`plan_round`, accepted plan, `demonstration_records`, verifier brief), none of which changes. Revision answers: (1) every demonstration is one plain `cargo test ...` command, because `demonstration_command` (verify.rs:717-730) refuses `&&` chains. (2) Test code never names the helper. Athena's revert run (verify.rs:872-949) puts base `run/mod.rs` back and keeps tests.rs, so a test naming the helper would not compile there. The trigger's cases are covered through `Athena::go` with fake readers instead. (3) The ordinary-job demonstration is declared a guard that also passes on the revert run. (4) The Behavior-only reason is corrected. (5) The stale doc lines are listed as dependents. (6) The open question is narrowed. (7) The plans test uses `behavior_plan(seam)` and the seam-mapped `cargo test --locked`.

decisions.choice: Put the trigger in a private `fn asks_for_failing_run(reading: &Reading) -> bool` in run/mod.rs, with a `///` doc comment and a const list of the four phrases. The gate passes `reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_failing_run(&reading)` to `JobPlanConfig::plans`. No test names the helper.
decisions.reason: The fault is the gate at mod.rs:804-809, which looks only at `hard_reason`, so an easy job gets no plan and demonstrations run only from an accepted plan (checks.rs demonstration_runs). A named, documented helper is what criterion 4 asks for. Because tests do not name it, Athena's revert run (verify.rs `revert_plan` puts base mod.rs back, keeps tests.rs) still compiles the tests, and the plans test fails on its own assertion, not on a compile error.

rejected.option: Change `JobPlanConfig::plans` to take the reading or a second bool
rejected.why: It would touch the config.rs `plans` tests, which criterion 6 says stay unchanged, and make config depend on reading text.

rejected.option: Set `hard_reason` on the reading when a criterion asks for a failing run
rejected.why: `hard_reason` also escalates the producer model and effort (reading.rs `producer_setting`, `producer_effort`), so it would change which model builds the job.

rejected.option: Add a `fails_without` field to the reading's Criterion record
rejected.why: Out of scope: it changes a record schema and the reader's output.

rejected.option: Plan every job with any Behavior criterion
rejected.why: Too broad. The CLI default reading has a Behavior criterion (tests/common/mod.rs:359), so most easy jobs would be planned and criterion 2 would fail.

rejected.option: A unit test that calls the helper directly
rejected.why: On Athena's revert copy the base mod.rs has no such function, so run::tests would not compile and could not show the plans test failing.

decisions.choice: Match only Behavior criteria, on lower-cased, whitespace-collapsed text, against the four fixed phrases.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading and criterion 4 limit the trigger to Behavior criteria whose text names 'fails without the fix'. The reading's Criterion has only `text` and `kind` (records.rs). Admission demands a seam and a `fails_without` from Behavior criteria only (admission.rs:199-201), so those are the criteria whose demonstration the plan must carry. A Content criterion can also carry a `fails_without` and such demonstrations do run (verify.rs `demonstration_groups` has no kind filter; the test at tests.rs:3128 runs one), but the brief scopes the trigger to Behavior, and a Content criterion that only mentions the phrase should not plan the job. The plural 'tests fail without the fix' already matches `fail without the fix`.

rejected.why: The brief scopes the trigger to Behavior criteria, and a Content criterion that only mentions the phrase would plan the job for no demonstration need.
It matches unrelated prose such as 'the build fails without a network'. Fixed phrases keep false triggers rare; a false trigger costs one planning round.

decisions.choice: Cover the trigger's cases through `Athena::go` with table-driven core tests: kinds and wordings that plan and ones that do not, including case, double spaces, the plural, a Content criterion naming the phrase, and unrelated 'fails without a network' text. Name the tests with the prefix `easy_job_planning_` so each demonstration's name filter selects what it should.
decisions.reason: This replaces the helper unit test. The cases are observed as planner and critic calls, through the real gate and a fake reader, and the tests compile on the reverted copy.

rejected.option: Make the helper `pub(crate)` and unit-test it
rejected.why: The test would not compile on Athena's revert copy.

rejected.option: Only one positive and one negative case
rejected.why: The matching rule would be untested on Content criteria, case and spacing, and unrelated text.

decisions.choice: The demonstration record `fails-without-1` reaching the verifier is asserted in the core test only. The CLI tests assert planning under the repository's real `[job_plan]` table.
decisions.reason: Core tests can install `demo_seam` (checks.rs, used at tests.rs:3098) and run a real revert copy. The CLI fixture has no seam, and `demo_seam` is crate-private, so exporting it would add surface the change does not need.

rejected.option: Install the demo seam in CLI tests
rejected.why: It needs a new public test-support export.

decisions.choice: Edit only doc comments in config.rs on `PlanMode::Hard` and `JobPlanConfig::plans`. Leave the `hard_reason` doc lines in records.rs:472-475, outputs.rs:43 and the reading.rs:4024 test comment unchanged.
decisions.reason: The config doc (config.rs:186 area) says hard mode plans only a hard reading, which would be false after the change; config.rs is a listed deliverable. The other three lines say what hard marking causes ('a hard job gets ... a planner and critic when mode is hard'), which stays true, and none says it is the only trigger. outputs.rs feeds the reader prompt set, which is at 1997 of 2000 tokens (system-facts budget line), so a wording change there risks the budget test `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` for no gain.

rejected.option: Reword records.rs and outputs.rs to mention the new trigger
rejected.why: They are not deliverables, and outputs.rs sits at the reader budget limit; they describe the reader's marking, which the new trigger does not use.
Its `PlanMode::Hard` doc would be wrong, and the deliverables list the file.

decisions.choice: Give each demonstration exactly one plain `cargo test ...` command with a test-name filter; criteria 1 and 3 share one command; criterion 6 uses `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test job_plan`. Content criteria (4, 5) carry no `fails_without`.
decisions.reason: `demonstration_command` returns None for any word with `|&;<>()$...` (verify.rs:717-730), and checks.rs:270-273 then records 'not a plain cargo test command' without running it. Commands group by identical text (verify.rs:734-757), so criteria 1 and 3 share one run, and with criteria 2 and 6 that makes three distinct commands, within `MAX_DEMONSTRATION_RUNS` = 3 (verify.rs:702).

rejected.why: Athena would not run them and no fails-without record would reach the verifier.

rejected.option: A fourth distinct command for a CLI revert run
rejected.why: It would exceed the three runs Athena makes; criterion 6's job_plan command carries the CLI revert run.

risks.risk: The phrase match over free text can fire on a criterion that mentions the phrase without really asking for a failing run, or miss a differently worded ask.
risks.mitigation: A false trigger costs one planning round. It is limited to Behavior criteria and fixed phrases, and `enabled = false` still switches planning off. Preflight reserves the planning budget before anything is committed, so an unaffordable job is held, not half-run. The wording table tests show what does and does not fire.

risks.risk: The core tests change the criterion text in the reader fake, but the producer and verifier fakes echo the old `CRITERION`, so the job could be sent back or rejected.
risks.mitigation: The wrapper rewrites the text in all three fakes (reader `acceptance_criteria`, producer `criteria_check`, verifier `criteria`), following the `run_planned_behavior` pattern at tests.rs:632. The plans test asserts the job lands, so a mismatch shows up as a failed job.

risks.risk: A Behavior criterion in an unplanned core job might be sent back or held for lacking a plan, which would make the skip tests fail for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: The CLI default reading already has a Behavior criterion and lands unplanned under hard mode (job_plan.rs:1104, tests/common/mod.rs:359), so the base accepts that shape. If the core fake path differs, the roles assertion names the cause.

risks.risk: The plans test's demonstration record appears only if the plan's command is a plain `cargo test ...` and the seam is installed; a mistake would make the prompt assertion fail for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: Use `behavior_plan(seam)` (command `cargo test --locked`, plain) and `demo_seam::install` with `README_TEST` as in tests.rs:3096-3125. The seam guard value is held for the whole job.

risks.risk: Athena's revert run shows the ordinary-job test passing, and the verifier might read that as missing evidence.
risks.mitigation: Criterion 2's demonstration states it is a guard that passes on the revert run and goes red only under the over-broad mutation.

risks.risk: The reverted copy fails to compile if any test names an item that exists only after the change.
risks.mitigation: Tests never name `asks_for_failing_run` or the phrase const; only tests.rs's own helpers are new. The producer's step 4 mutation edits only the gate line, which matches the compile state of Athena's revert.

risks.risk: `repo_with_config` strips the `[job_plan]` table from athena.toml, and a wrong key would fail the config parse (`deny_unknown_fields`).
risks.mitigation: Build `repo_with_hard_planning` from the exact text of `repo_with_planning` (tests.rs:283-288) with `mode = "hard"`.

risks.risk: Criterion 6's revert run of the job_plan target may take long against `check_timeout_s`.
risks.mitigation: The command is a single integration target with a name-free filter; if it times out Athena records that run, and the producer's full `cargo test --locked` result still stands in step 7.
